## Funding opportunity: EPSRC standard research grant, Nov 2023: responsive mode
Opportunity status:
Open
Funders:
Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)
Funding type:
Grant
Publication date:
13 November 2023
Opening date:
13 November 2023 9:00am UK time
Closing date:
Open - no closing date
Last updated: 7 October 2025 - see all updates
Standard research grants are available for researchers at eligible research organisations.
There is no limit on the value of the grant or length of the project. You should ask for what is needed to deliver the proposed programme of research.
Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) will award 80% of the full economic cost (FEC) of the project.
For information on our new approach to EPSRC responsive mode opportunities that opened in November 2023, please see our transition pages .

## Who can apply
Before applying for funding, check the Eligibility of your organisation .
Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) standard eligibility rules apply. For full details, visit EPSRC’s eligibility page .
UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) has introduced new role types for funding opportunities being run on the new UKRI Funding Service.
For full details, visit Eligibility as an individual

## International applicants
Under the UKRI and Research Council of Norway Money Follows Cooperation agreement a project co-lead (international) (previously co-investigator) can be based in a Norwegian institution.

## Resubmissions
We will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UKRI or any other funder.
Find out more about EPSRC’s resubmissions policy .

## Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants.
We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
• career breaks
• support for people with caring responsibilities
• flexible working
• alternative working patterns
Find out more about equality, diversity and inclusion at UKRI .

## What we're looking for

## Aim
We are committed to the continued support of excellent discovery led research as detailed in EPSRC’s strategic delivery plan 2022 to 2025 .
Through EPSRC standard research grants we fund a wide range of projects, from small, short-term grants to multi-million-pound research projects including:
• high-risk or high-return research embracing new concepts or techniques
• feasibility studies
• instrument development
• project specific equipment
• collaborative projects that cross different disciplines

## Scope
You can apply for a standard research grant in any field of research relevant to our remit. We support high quality research in:
• artificial intelligence (AI)
• digital security and resilience
• energy and decarbonisation
• engineering
• healthcare technologies
• information and communication technologies (ICT)
• manufacturing and the circular economy
• mathematical sciences
• physical sciences
• quantum technologies
Find out more about our research areas and themes .

## Critical technologies
EPSRC particularly welcomes high quality applications where engineering and physical sciences research can generate new knowledge and addresses challenges associated with the advancement, development, and deployment of these technologies as follows:
• artificial intelligence (AI): machines that perform tasks normally performed by human intelligence, especially when the machines learn from data how to do those tasks
• engineering biology: the application of rigorous engineering principles to the design of biological systems
• future telecommunications: evolutions of the infrastructure for digitised data and communications
• semiconductors: a class of electronic materials with unique properties that sit at the heart of the devices and technology we use every day
• quantum technologies: devices and systems which rely on quantum mechanics, to provide capabilities that ‘classical’ machines cannot
Applications for research addressing these areas should ensure complementarity with existing funding, including via strategic initiatives in the area and where applicable existing UKRI strategies.
Applications received will be considered on their scientific and engineering merit in competition with all other applications. The signpost will not be used to change the rank order of proposals for funding.
The majority of your research must fall within our remit.
We will work with other research councils to ensure that applications close to remit boundaries are assessed by the most appropriate lead council. We encourage you to contact us first to discuss your application if you believe your research may cross research council boundaries.
See our remit query form .

## Duration
There is no limit on the length of your project. Awards made via this opportunity will have a fixed start date if the award is valued over £3,000,000 full economic cost.

## Funding available
There is no limit on the value of the grant.
We will fund 80% FEC of your project.

## What we will fund
We will fund:
• staff costs
• equipment (up to £400,000 per item)
• other items required to carry out the project
• costs related to impact
• travel and subsistence
Quotes for equipment do not need to be included in your application, but please retain quotes for equipment costing more than £138,000 as we may ask for these at post-panel stage before releasing funds.

## Supporting skills and talent
We encourage you to follow the principles of the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers and the Technician Commitment .

## International collaboration
If your application includes international applicants, project partners or collaborators, visit UKRI trusted research and innovation for more information on effective international collaboration.
Find out about getting funding for international collaboration .

## How to apply
EPSRC reviewed its approach to responsive mode opportunities on the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Funding Service following our October 2023 closing dates. For more information on our approach, including timelines, please see our transition web pages .
From November 2023, our approach to responsive mode will change. We will not publish closing dates for individual rounds, instead we will batch applications internally. You should apply when their application is ready for submission and not be concerned about a closing date.
Due to systems requirements a closing date will appear on the Funding Service approximately 28 months from the publication of this opportunity.
Please do not wait for this date to submit your application, we will be processing applications throughout 2024, 2025 and 2026.
Applications will be batched for assessment and sent to the most appropriate responsive mode panel meeting when they reach this stage of the process. Our responsive mode panel meetings are: Engineering, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), Mathematical Sciences, and Physical Sciences. These panels are expected to run on a quarterly basis after September 2024.
Due to the agile development of the Funding Service, we will need to make changes to this opportunity to allow technical updates or new policies to be implemented. No changes are planned to EPSRC responsive mode opportunities before March 2026. However, if updates are required, we will communicate these changes at least eight weeks before they are implemented (excluding major public holiday periods).
We are running this funding opportunity on the new Funding Service. You cannot apply on the Joint Electronic Submissions (Je-S) system.
The project lead is responsible for completing the application process on the UKRI Funding Service, but we expect all team members and project partners to contribute to the application.
Only the lead research organisation can submit an application to UKRI. You cannot submit applications with more than one lead organisation.
To apply:
Select ‘Start application’ near the beginning of this Funding finder page.
• Confirm you are the project lead.
• Sign in or create a Funding Service account. To create an account, select your organisation, verify your email address, and set a password. If your organisation is not listed, email support@funding-service.ukri.org
• Answer questions directly in the text boxes. You can save your answers and come back to complete them or work offline and return to copy and paste your answers. If we need you to upload a document, follow the upload instructions in the Funding Service. All questions and assessment criteria are listed in the How to apply section on this Funding finder page.
• Send the completed application to your research office for checking. They will return it to you if it needs editing.
• Your research office will submit the completed and checked application to UKRI.
Find out more about How applicants use the Funding Service and also How research offices use the Funding Service .
We will not be returning applications for amendment. If an application is withdrawn prior to peer review or office rejected due to substantive errors in the application then you will need to submit a new application.

## Personal data

## Processing personal data
EPSRC as part of UKRI, will need to collect some personal information to manage your Funding Service account and the registration of your funding applications.
We will handle personal data in line with UK data protection legislation and manage it securely. For more information, including how to exercise your rights, read our privacy notice .

## Institutional matched funding
There is no requirement for matched funding from the institutions hosting the project lead, project co-leads or other staff employed on the application, beyond the standard 20% FEC. Expert reviewers and panels assessing UKRI funding applications must not consider levels of institutional matched funding as a factor on which to base recommendations. Direct and in-kind contributions from third party project partners are encouraged.
This policy does not remove the need for support from host organisations who must provide the necessary research environment and infrastructure for award-specific activities funded by UKRI. For example, research facilities, training and development of staff.

## Publication of outcomes
EPSRC, as part of UKRI, will publish the outcomes of this funding opportunity.
If your application is successful, we will publish some personal information on the UKRI Gateway to Research .

## Summary
Word count: maximum 550
In plain English, provide a summary we can use to identify the most suitable experts to assess your application.
We may make this summary publicly available on external-facing websites, so make it suitable for a variety of readers, for example:
• opinion-formers
• policymakers
• the public
• the wider research community

## Guidance for writing a summary
Clearly describe your proposed work in terms of:
• context
• the challenge the project addresses
• aims and objectives
• potential applications and benefits

## Core team
List the key members of your team and assign them roles from the following:
• project lead (PL)
• project co-lead (UK) (PcL)
• project co-lead (international) (PcL (I))
• researcher co-lead (RcL)
• specialist
• grant manager
• professional enabling staff
• research and innovation associate
• technician
• visiting researcher
Only list one individual as project lead.
The project co-lead (international) (PcL (I)) role should only be used for applications making use of the UKRI-RCN Money Follows Cooperation agreement or the UKRI-IIASA agreement. EPSRC does not otherwise accept project co-lead (international) applicants.
Find out more about UKRI’s new grant roles .

## Thematic area alignment
Word count: 1
Select the EPSRC thematic area your application most closely aligns to. This should be the theme where the majority of the novelty in the research lies.
In the text box, copy the letter corresponding to your selected theme:
A. artificial intelligence (AI) B. digital security and resilience C. energy and decarbonisation D. engineering E. healthcare technologies F. information and communication technologies (ICT) G. manufacturing H. mathematical sciences I. physical sciences J. quantum technologies
If you are applying as part of the critical technologies signpost please add the number 1 after your theme letter (with no space).

## Additional guidance
This is for administrative purposes to help the initial application processing. We will check your choice and make a final decision on which theme will lead the peer review of your application.
We will not publish closing dates for individual rounds, instead we will batch applications internally. You should apply when your application is ready for submission and not be concerned about a closing date.
Applications will be batched for assessment and sent to the most appropriate responsive mode panel meeting when they reach this stage of the process.

## Vision and Approach
Create a document that includes your responses to all criteria. The document should not be more than six sides of A4, single spaced in paper in 11-point Arial (or equivalent sans serif font) with margins of at least 2cm. You may include images, graphs, tables. You can have an additional one page for a diagrammatic workplan.
For the file name, use the unique Funding Service number the system gives you when you create an application, followed by the words ‘Vision and Approach’.
Save this document as a single PDF file, no bigger than 8MB. Unless specifically requested, please do not include any personal data within the attachment.
If the attachment does not meet these requirements, the application will be rejected.
The Funding Service will provide document upload details when you apply.
What are you hoping to achieve with and how will you deliver your proposed work?

## What the assessors are looking for in your response
For the Vision, explain how your proposed work:
• is of excellent quality and importance within or beyond the field(s) or area(s)
• has the potential to advance current understanding, generates new knowledge, thinking or discovery within or beyond the field or area
• is timely given current trends, context and needs
• impacts world-leading research, society, the economy or the environment
Within the Vision section we also expect you to:
• identify the potential direct or indirect benefits and who the beneficiaries might be
For the Approach, explain how you have designed your work so that it:
• is effective and appropriate to achieve your objectives
• is feasible, and comprehensively identifies any risks to delivery and how they will be managed
• if applicable, uses a clear and transparent methodology
• if applicable, summarises the previous work and describes how this will be built upon and progressed
• will maximise translation of outputs into outcomes and impacts
• describes how your, and if applicable your team’s, research environment (in terms of the place, and relevance to the project) will contribute to the success of the work
Within the Approach section we also expect you to:
• demonstrate access to the appropriate services, facilities, infrastructure, or equipment to deliver the proposed work
• provide a project plan including milestones and timelines in the form of a Gantt chart or similar (additional one-page A4)

## Applicant and team capability to deliver
Word count: 1,500
Why are you the right individual or team to successfully deliver the proposed work?
Evidence of how you, and if relevant your team, have:
• the relevant experience (appropriate to career stage) to deliver the proposed work
• the right balance of skills and expertise to cover the proposed work
• the appropriate leadership and management skills to deliver the work and your approach to develop others
[text shortened]

scheme-leverhulme-research-project-grant.text:
I found the current state, but some details are missing. I used up my search and fetch limit before I could open the Outline Application Help Notes or the FAQs. So I can't confirm the page or word limits, the CV format, or whether letters are needed. The direct fetch of the main page returned an old saved copy from September 2025. The 2026 facts below come from search snippets of the Trust's own pages.

**Fit for you:** Recommend. It's open to any topic and realistic for an early-career lead applicant. Fit score is 78 (strong). At least 75% of the budget must go on research staff, which suits hiring a postdoc. The Trust excludes research aimed mainly at an immediate commercial use, so frame the offshore-wind work as fundamental science.

## Is a round open now (22 Nov 2026)?
- **Yes, for outline applications. They are accepted at any time, with no deadline.** They reopened in the new grant system on "Monday 21 September 2026".
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/leverhulme-grant-system-update (published "01 September 2026")
- The Trust's closing-dates table lists "Research Project Grants – Outline Applications | No deadline". It also says "All deadlines are 4pm (UK time) unless otherwise specified."
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/closing-dates
- **The deadlines for full ("detailed") applications in 2027 are not published anywhere I could see.** Only invited applicants can submit one, after their outline is approved. The main page says "Page last updated: 21 September 2026" and refers to "changes to what the Trust offers". I couldn't see what those changes are.
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-project-grants
- Outline assessment "is normally completed within three months". This comes from the September 2025 copy of the main page, so it may have changed.

## Previous round
- Outlines were paused at a deadline of "27 February 2026, 4pm". Outcomes were due "by 30 April 2026". Anyone invited "between 1 December 2025 and 30 April 2026" had to submit by "1 September 2026".
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/RPG2026
- Detailed-application deadlines were "1 December 2025, 4pm Decision: March 2026", "1 July 2026, 4pm Decision: October 2026" and "1 September 2026, 4pm Decision: December 2026". There was no March 2026 deadline.
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/detailed-applications-research-project-grants-0
- The main page gives the decision dates differently in two places:
  - "1 July 2026 (Mid-October) 1 September 2026 (Late-November)".
  - Elsewhere it says decisions for applications submitted "on or before 1 September 2026 will be announced by the beginning of December 2026".
  - Earliest start dates: "1 July 2026 closing date: 1 November 2026"; "1 September 2026 closing date: 1 December 2026".
  - https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-project-grants

## Next round expected
- The 2027 detailed-application deadlines are not confirmed. In 2025 the main page said "deadlines are the same every year" (March, September and December), but the 2026 move to the new system broke that pattern. I won't guess the 2027 dates.
- My advice is to submit an outline by about early February 2027. With roughly three months for assessment, that should give you an invitation in time for a mid-2027 deadline, whenever it is announced.

## Eligibility
All from https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-project-grants unless marked otherwise.
- **Institution:** "UK universities and other institution of higher education in the UK". Some UK museums and charities can also apply.
- **Applicant:** must "already be employed by the eligible institution". People on research contracts can apply if the contract lasts at least as long as the grant.
- **Career stage, years since PhD, nationality:** no limits are stated. You are eligible.
- **Co-applicants:** "Up to 3 co-applicants"; "Overseas co-applicants are allowable."
- **Topics excluded:** disease and clinical work; advocacy; policy evidence-gathering; work "aimed principally at an immediate commercial application"; mainly building databases; and "capacity building, networking, or the development of the skills" of those involved.
- **Not allowed:** continuation funding for an existing Leverhulme grant.

## Award amount and duration
- **Amount:** "The maximum grant value is £500,000." This is from the September 2025 copy. Oxford's 2026 page also says £500,000 (https://www.politics.ox.ac.uk/opportunity/open-leverhulme-trust-research-project-grants). I couldn't confirm the current main page.
- **Duration:** "a minimum of six months, up to five years" (current main page).
- **Budget rules** (September 2025 copy; may be among the changes):
  - At least 75% must go on research staff (research assistants or PhD students).
  - At least one of them must spend at least 50% of their time on the project.
  - Other research costs are capped at 25%.
  - Teaching replacement of up to 33% is allowed for staff with continuing contracts, which you are.
  - No salary for you or your co-applicants.

## What you must submit
- **Stage 1, outline:** submit through the "Leverhulme Grant System", using the "Outline Application Help Notes" (current main page). The 2025 page said to save a PDF of your outline, as it won't be available afterwards.
- **Stage 2, detailed application:** by invitation only. It must be "an elaboration of the Outline". The aims can't change significantly, and the budget can change only for pay-scale updates.
- **Things the Trust says reviewers look at:** your personal vision, risk-taking, work across disciplines, and why Leverhulme is the right funder.
- **Feedback:** none is given on unsuccessful applications.
- **Not confirmed:** section lists, page or word limits, CV format, letters of support, head-of-department statements. These are in the Help Notes, which I couldn't open.
- **Internal selection:** the Trust doesn't mention one. Your university may still have its own internal deadline (Oxford asks for five days), so check with Manchester's research office.

## Next steps
1. Read the new Outline Application Help Notes and the "changes" section on the main page.
2. Register on the new Leverhulme Grant System and draft an outline, aiming for early February 2027.
3. Tell Manchester's research office and agree the costing with the finance office.

scheme-leverhulme-philip-leverhulme-priz.text:
I couldn't confirm the requirements in full. The Leverhulme site wouldn't load directly and my tool limit ran out, so the notes below come from search-engine copies of the Trust's pages, plus some university and third-party pages, which I've labelled. Treat dates as needing a check on the live page.

**Bottom line for you:** this isn't worth pursuing in 2027. The 2027 subjects don't include Engineering, and Engineering comes back in 2028. You can only be nominated in one subject per 3-year cycle, so a 2027 Physics or Earth Sciences nomination would rule you out of Engineering in 2028. You're eligible on years since PhD, but you need clear international impact, so 2028 would still be a stretch.

**Is a round open now (22 Nov 2026)?**
- No. The page shows "Currently closed", with "Decision: **November 2026**" for the 2026 round. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- The 2027 closing date only says "2027", with no day given. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/closing-dates
- "Schemes at a glance" says "Currently closed". A nearby line reads "Next round opens 1 January 2027", but the snippet was jumbled, so I can't confirm that date belongs to this prize. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/schemes-at-a-glance
- I couldn't confirm the 2027 opening date, closing date or time.

**Previous round (2026)**
- Closing date: "4pm on Wednesday 14 May 2026" (Trust's 2026 guidance PDF, copy hosted by Worcester). — https://researchfunding.on.worc.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026_PLPguidance_0-4.pdf
  - 14 May 2026 was actually a Thursday, so the PDF has a mistake somewhere.
- The 2026 prize page also says "the closing date of 14 May 2026". — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- Referees' deadline was 1 June 2026 (third-party site only, not confirmed by the Trust). — https://www.granthub.co/grants/call-for-entries-philip-leverhulme-prize-united-kingdom
- Results: 30 winners announced, "Chosen from over 400 nominations". — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/2026PLP
- Cambridge set an internal deadline of 3 March 2026. — https://neuroscience.cam.ac.uk/restricted-call-leverhulme-trust-philip-leverhulme-prizes-2026-internal-deadline-3rd-march-2026/

**Next round**
- 2027 subjects: Classics, Earth Sciences, Physics, Politics and International Relations, Psychology, and Visual and Performing Arts. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/news/2026PLP and https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- 2028 subjects: Archaeology, Chemistry, Economics, **Engineering**, Geography, Languages and Literatures. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- The page says "The current cycle is 2026, 2027 and 2028. You may not be nominated for more than one prize subject in any 3-year cycle." — same page
- My estimate from past rounds: it opens around January and closes mid-May, at 4pm.
  - 2022 round: opened January 2022 and closed "17 May 2022 (16:00)" (Newcastle University blog). — https://microsites.ncl.ac.uk/nubsstaffblog/?p=12836
  - 2025 round: "Deadline is 14th May" (Manchester Met blog). — https://mmuresearchblog.wordpress.com/2025/02/27/philip-leverhulme-prize/
- It runs every year ("Annual"). — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/schemes-at-a-glance

**Who is eligible**
- Researchers early in their careers "whose work has had international impact and whose future research career is exceptionally promising". — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/schemes-at-a-glance
- Years since PhD: should "normally" be no more than ten years before the closing date. The degree date is the one on the certificate. The only exceptions are career breaks for caring responsibilities or illness. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- Post: you must hold a permanent post or long-term fellowship at a UK university with research degree awarding powers, lasting beyond the prize. People without a salary aren't eligible. — 2026 guidance PDF (Worcester copy, above); the Trust's own page also says "Those otherwise without salary are not eligible".
- Nomination: by your head of department (or equivalent). Each institution can nominate at most three people per subject. Prizes go to individuals, and the Trust won't fund two nominations for substantially the same work. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- The Trust doesn't fund medical or clinical research. — 2026 guidance PDF
- I found no nationality rule.

**Amount and duration**
- £100,000, spent over 2 to 3 years. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/schemes-at-a-glance and https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- Start date: the first of a month between 1 December of the award year and 1 November the following year. — https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes
- Paid to your employer in two equal instalments (Cambridge page only). — Cambridge link above
- It can be spent on research assistance, teaching replacement, travel and subsistence, consumables, technical support, and computer equipment and software (Worcester page). — https://researchfunding.on.worc.ac.uk/?p=2155

**What you must submit (only partly confirmed)**
- A nomination from your head of department, sent through the Trust's Grants Management System. Your institution must approve and submit it by the deadline. — 2026 guidance PDF
- The guidance mentions "a letter of nomination", but the rest of that section was cut off.
- References from referees (third-party site only).
- An internal selection round at your university, because of the cap of three per subject. Manchester's internal deadline isn't known.
- **Not confirmed:** page or word limits, CV or publication-list format, number of referees, and any personal statement. Check the full "Guidance for Nominees" PDF on the prize page.

**Next steps**
1. Wait for the 2028 Engineering round rather than using your one nomination on Physics or Earth Sciences in 2027.
2. Ask Manchester's research office about its internal selection timing for 2028.
3. Before then, build evidence of international impact: invited talks, prizes and citations.

scheme-leverhulme-research-fellowships.text:
The 2027 round of Leverhulme Research Fellowships closed at 4pm on 5 November 2026, so nothing is open today (22 November 2026). I don't recommend it for you: it's aimed at experienced researchers whose teaching has held back their research, and you're about a year into a Lecturer post after a research-only fellowship.

**I couldn't get current information from Leverhulme's own website.** The tool returned a copy of https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-fellowships saved on 18 October 2025, which is the version for the earlier round. My other requests to leverhulme.ac.uk were blocked by a usage limit. So the round dates and the £70,000 figure below come from other websites that repeat Leverhulme's information. Please check them on the Trust's site before relying on them.

**Round status**
- **Current round:** the 2027 round is closed. It was open through the new Leverhulme Grant System and closed "at 4pm on 5 November 2026". Sources: https://www.dementiaresearcher.nihr.ac.uk/funding/leverhulme-research-fellowships-2027/ and https://opportunitiesforyouth.org/2026/09/18/leverhulme-trust-research-fellowships-2027-up-to-70000-for-experienced-researchers-in-any-discipline/
- **Opening date:** not confirmed. Other websites were reporting the round as open by 18–19 September 2026.
- **Previous round (2026):** I couldn't find its dates.
- **Next round:** not announced. Leverhulme says it offers about 100 fellowships "each year" (Leverhulme page above), so a 2028 round probably opens around September 2027 and closes in early November 2027. That is my estimate from this year's dates only.

**Eligibility** (https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-fellowships, October 2025 copy)
- **Career stage:** for "experienced researchers". You must have "an established track record in their chosen area of research".
- **Priority:** goes to people whose teaching and administrative duties have "significantly impacted their ability to undertake research in the three years prior to their application".
- **Years since PhD:** the page sets no limit.
- **Institution:** you must hold a post at a UK university with research degree awarding powers, and the post must last beyond the end of the fellowship.
- **Residence:** you must be "resident in the UK at the time of application" and be "a permanent member of the UK scholarly community". The page sets no nationality rule.
- **Not eligible:**
  - independent scholars;
  - anyone registered for, or waiting to be examined for, a degree;
  - anyone whose post is "wholly or predominantly research focused" when they apply;
  - applications where the main cost is research assistance.
- **Subjects excluded:** studies of human or animal disease, and research meant to inform clinical practice.
- **Limits on applying:** one application per round. A second award needs at least seven years since the previous application. You can't apply for an International Fellowship and a Research Fellowship in the same year.

**Award**
- **Amount:** "£70,000" maximum for the 2027 round (dementiaresearcher and opportunitiesforyouth pages above). The October 2025 copy of Leverhulme's page says £65,000.
- **Length:** 3 to 24 months. You must spend at least 75% of your time on the project.
- **Start date:** between 1 June of the award year and 1 May of the following year.
- **What it pays for:** research expenses and "a contribution towards reasonable replacement costs" for someone to cover your duties.

**What you must submit** (Leverhulme page, October 2025 copy)
- An online application through the Leverhulme grants system. The page also refers to separate Application Help Notes and a Guidance for Applicants PDF.
- A "Detailed Statement of Proposed Research". **I couldn't confirm its page or word limit, the CV format, or whether referees are needed**, because the Help Notes didn't load.
- Your head of department must fully agree with the application's content.
- Your university's approver must confirm your release time, your salary during the award, and any replacement-cost and research-expense requests.
- The Trust "strongly recommends" sending the application for university approval at least five working days before the closing date.
- The page mentions no internal selection by universities. No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants.

**Fit for you:** it's open to any topic, but you're probably too early in your career for it. You were in a research-only fellowship until 2025, so you can't yet show three years of heavy teaching and admin. You also hold a New Investigator Award. The Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship (closes 4pm on 18 February 2027) is worth considering instead, but only as a host for a postdoc, which you said you want to do.

**Next steps**
1. Check the £70,000 figure and the 2028 round dates on leverhulme.ac.uk.
2. Look at this scheme again around 2029, once you have a record of heavy teaching.
3. Find a candidate for a Leverhulme Early Career Fellowship to host before 18 February 2027.

scheme-leverhulme-early-career-fellowshi.text:
I couldn't open the Leverhulme page directly: the fetch was refused and then I hit my tool-use limit. The Leverhulme facts below come from search-engine copies of two leverhulme.ac.uk pages. Where only a university page or a third-party site had the information, I say so.

**Verdict: don't apply. You aren't eligible, for two separate reasons.**
1. **Your permanent post.** Lancaster's summary of the rules says applicants must not yet have held a full-time permanent academic post in a UK university or comparable UK institution. Your 2025 permanent lectureship rules you out. I couldn't see this line in the copy of the Leverhulme page itself, but Oxford and Manchester list the same rule.
2. **The four-year window since your thesis.** Those who formally submitted their doctoral thesis for viva voce examination before 18 February 2023 are not eligible unless they have since had a career break (https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/early-career-fellowships). Your DPhil was awarded in 2022, so you almost certainly submitted before that date.

This is a postdoc fellowship. A postdoc could hold one in your group (Manchester can host), but each school has its own internal deadline. Biological Sciences' was Friday 23 October 2026, so ask Engineering what theirs is.

**Is a round open, and when?** (as of 22 Nov 2026)
- **Closing date:** applications must be approved and submitted to the Trust by the host university by 4pm on the closing date of 18 February 2027. The Trust's closing-dates page also lists Early Career Fellowships | 18 February 2027. Sources: https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/early-career-fellowships and https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/closing-dates
- **Opening date:** not confirmed on the Trust's site. University pages say 1 January 2027 · Leverhulme online application form opens. (https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/humanities-arts-and-social-sciences/research/leverhulme-trust-early-career-fellowships/). So it isn't open yet; universities are running internal selection now.
- **Start dates:** A Fellowship must commence between 1 September 2027 and 1 May 2028. (Leverhulme page)
- **Previous round:** the only source I found is a third-party site, which gives 4pm on the closing date of 19 February 2026 (grantedai.com). Not confirmed on the Trust's site.
- **Next round after this one:** not stated anywhere. The round runs every year (Oxford says the deadline is usually in February each year), so I'd expect roughly January to February 2028. That's my estimate, not something announced.

**Eligibility** (Leverhulme page, https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/early-career-fellowships)
- **Doctorate:** you must have submitted their doctoral thesis for viva voce examination by 4pm on the closing date of 18 February 2027, with the four-year window quoted above.
- **UK connection:** applicants must either hold a degree (any degree) from a UK higher education institution at the time of taking up the Fellowship or at the time of the application deadline must hold an academic position in the UK. That position must have started at least 4 months before the closing date.
- **Nationality:** I couldn't find a nationality rule.
- **Limits:** A candidate may submit only one application per year. Earlier unsuccessful applicants may reapply.
- **Excluded topics** (Manchester's page): studies of disease in humans and animals, and research meant to inform clinical practice.

**Award**
- **Duration:** Fellowships are tenable for 3 years on a full-time basis.
- **Number:** Approximately 145 Fellowships are available in 2027.
- **Amount:** not confirmed. I couldn't see the Trust's figures for salary contribution or research expenses.
- **Matching funding:** a third-party copy of the 2026 rules says The host department must secure the matching funding for the applicant before the closing date.

**What to submit**
- **Online form:** application through the Trust's online system, submitted by the host university (Leverhulme page).
- **References:** referees give their references through the online system after you apply (third-party copy of the 2026 rules).
- **Internal selection:** host universities run their own shortlisting first. Leeds, for example, says we operate a mandatory internal shortlisting and selection process for this scheme.
- **Not confirmed:** section headings, word or page limits, CV format and any required statements. I couldn't reach the Trust's guidance notes.

**Next steps**
1. Don't apply yourself.
2. Ask Manchester Engineering for its internal deadline if you want to sponsor a postdoc.
3. Check the amount and form limits on the Leverhulme page once it opens on 1 January 2027.

scheme-ice-rd-enabling-fund.text:
I couldn't confirm most of what you asked for. The ICE fund page refused a direct fetch and I hit the tool limit, so everything below comes from search-engine copies of ICE pages. The main page copy was 18 days old. I never saw the call themes, the application form or the guidance.

**Status of the current round**
- **Open now. It opened on 1 November 2026 and closes on 30 December 2026.** The page says the fund "will reopen for applications on 1 November 2026. Applications will remain open until 30 December 2026, after which all eligible submissions will be reviewed by the Panel." No closing time is given. — https://www.ice.org.uk/get-involved/awards-and-grants/research-and-development-enabling-fund
- **The page contradicts itself.** The same page also says the panel "will assess each application (there are no deadlines to apply) and aim to make a decision within one month of submission." The 30 December date is newer, so treat it as the deadline. — same URL
- ICE encourages people to prepare early and submit before the closing date. — same URL

**Previous round and next round**
- **Previous round dates: I couldn't confirm them.** Nothing on ICE's site that I could reach gives them. A third-party page from 2018 mentions a call in June 2018, which is too old to be useful.
- **Next round: not announced.** The page says each year the panel picks key topics and issues a call, so it probably runs yearly. I couldn't confirm when the next round opens. — same URL

**Who can apply**
- **Career stage, years since PhD, nationality: not stated** in anything I saw.
- **ICE membership: probably not needed.** A 2023 ICE news item says the fund supports "ICE members and non-members". The 2018 third-party page said applicants should be ICE members, so check the current guidance. — https://www.ice.org.uk/news-views-insights/latest-news/study-seeks-members-insights-on-carbon-management
- **Your project must benefit ICE members.** It is judged against the year's call themes, of which there are three. I couldn't see what this year's themes are. — main URL

**Money and duration**
- **Up to £25,000 at first, for work that directly answers one or more of the three call themes.** ICE allows more in exceptional cases, up to £50,000 in total, "e.g. where findings from initial work demonstrate a clear need". — main URL
- **Payment is in stages:** money is released when key project milestones are met. — main URL
- **Duration: not stated.**

**What you must submit**
- **I couldn't confirm any of it.** I saw no sections, page or word limits, CV format, letters, statements or internal selection step. These are probably in a guidance document and application form linked from the main page.

**Assessment for you**
- **Topic fit: unclear until you see this year's three themes.** It's a civil engineering fund. Offshore wind foundations and coastal flood-protection work could fit if the themes cover infrastructure resilience or net zero. Engineering-led machine learning probably won't fit without that link.

## Innovation Calls
searching for novel solutions to help deliver offshore wind faster, cheaper and at lower risk

## Innovation call 2 - closed 9 April 2025
PROJECT SPONSORSHIP up to £300,000
Get access to

## Technology demonstration sites

## Funding application support

## Growing market opportunities
The Offshore Wind R&I Programme will sponsor innovative projects to bring new solutions to market, exploring ways to overcome the technical challenges of offshore wind development, build operational capacity and scale up activities.
We aim to give you the tools you need to support the build out of offshore wind projects throughout Scotland, the UK and further afield, whilst embedding economic benefits close to windfarm development.
Find out more about the programme and innovation call 2 (now closed for applications) in our webinar which was held on 13 March 2025. Slide deck and Q&A report are available to download here .
CALL 2 WEBINAR

## What we’re looking for
We’re looking for innovation projects offering solutions to key challenges areas .
Proposed projects should:
• offer a clear innovation (i.e. the programme will not fund services that can already be procured from the market);
• provide a clear and justifiable benefit to the innovation call sponsor(s);
• have potential to bring wider benefits across the offshore wind sector, supply chain, and Scottish and UK economy.
• be up to two years’ duration.
It is not the intention of EMEC or the R&I Programme to own any existing IP from the ideas submitted or the projects supported. However, call sponsor(s) may require specific arrangements (e.g. preferential commercial terms or ownership of specific documents created) to be made with the Sponsored Projects to ensure there is mutual benefit following the sponsorship. Please refer to call 2 terms and conditions for more details.
For full eligibility criteria, download our Scope and Guidance .
Scope and Guidance
CALL 2 T&Cs

## Application process and timings
The table below summarises the timescales for applying for call 2.
Call 2 launch
Wed 26 Feb 2025
Call 2 webinar
Thurs 13 Mar 2025
Stage 1 - Application
Queries: Submit queries five working days before the application deadline.
Wed 2 Apr 2025
Deadline: Application must be submitted via our online application form .
1pm, Wed 9 Apr 2025
Applicants notified of outcomes

For full overview of the application process, download our Scope and Guidance .

## Key impact criteria
• Relevance to challenge area
• Genuinely innovative
• Technical feasibility
• Project deliverability
• Benefit to call sponsor(s), including impact on project schedule/timescales, costs, operations, and project deliverability
• Funding request and value for money
• Benefit to wider offshore wind sector
• Scottish and UK benefit, including impact on supply chain capacity
• Risk assessment, mitigations and potential impacts on call sponsor safety, reputation and assets

## What's on offer

## Project sponsorship up to £1 million
Platinum Sponsor, West of Orkney Windfarm, is funding the R&I Programme up to £1 million.
Up to £300k sponsorship is available for the second innovation call however additional funding may be made available to those with the potential to have the biggest impact on the wind farm.
Candidates must detail the budget required for project completion and source of external funds that have already been secured. Funding intensity will range from 10% to 100% and is at the discretion of the Programme Governance Group. Funding intensity towards each project will be based upon:
• maturity of the project
• quality of the application
• relevance to the call sponsor.
See Scope and Guidance for full details.

## Support with project proposal
Each application will undergo preliminary screening. From experience, EMEC expects submissions to the programme to be at varying levels of maturity and credibility.
If progressing to detailed project proposal stage of the R&I Programme, EMEC will offer support to develop your proposal and collate required evidence. This may be via a physical or online workshop. Where deemed necessary, funding may be provided to support the development of a more comprehensive plan for promising ideas.

## Support with accessing alternative grant funding
Depending on the requirements and merits of the proposed innovation, EMEC may offer support to leverage grant funding and public support.
This may include in-house support to scope out an idea and/or develop a funding application or facilitating research into the potential of the idea and the associated costs and benefits.

## Support in demonstrating technologies
EMEC operates consented areas of sea-space for demonstrating offshore technologies, tools and techniques, as well as onshore facilities for energy system demonstrations. Access to these facilities to demonstrate innovations may awarded where relevant.
Find out more about EMEC’s test and demonstration facilities .

## Recognition and access to market
Project sponsorship should help leverage additional public and private investment into your innovation projects, to maximise its potential impact on call sponsors and offshore wind sector.
If the innovation proves to be a game-changer in the offshore wind sector, there is a huge client base (including the call sponsor and other ScotWind and INTOG lease areas) who may be interested in your product and service.

## Closed innovation calls
Call 1 closed for applications in February 2024.
The first call looked for solutions to address at least one of the following challenges:

## Metocean
Wind, waves and current

## Challenge
Understand the wind, wave and current conditions on site and en route

## Aims
Inform major decisions regarding installation and O&M including vessel choice and the activities that can be performed within well-understood weather windows.

## Deadline
Applications to be received by 1:00pm, Mon 12 Feb 2024

## Transportation & Installation
Design for short window installation
Maximise installation opportunities
Streamline requirements and processes to shorten required weather windows and allow highest probability of successful installation.
Our first innovation call is supporting three pioneering projects that will enhance offshore wind operations through advanced metocean intelligence, real-time wave prediction, and high-frequency radar for more accurate weather data.
Find out more about the projects supported through call 1.
Sponsored projects
Our second innovation call is looking for solutions to address the following challenges:

## Weather forecasting
Understanding site and metocean
The West of Orkney Windfarm is characterised by persistent periods of high wind speeds and sea states. Some offshore activities for the construction and operational phases can only be done in the gaps (weather windows) between times of strong wind and/or high waves. Being able to reliably forecast weather windows at short (minutes to hours) to long (weeks, months and seasons) ranges can improve safety, operations and reduce costs.
Improve the quality of weather forecasts, specifically weather windows, at the project site and its cable, ports and transit routes, using advances in live metocean measurements, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This will allow better weather-sensitive operational decisions to be made during surveys, construction, and operations and maintenance.
Applications to be received by 1:00pm, Wed 09 Apr 2025

## SOV design for turbine access
O&M, vessel design and supply
West of Orkney Windfarm is in a particularly challenging ocean environment with an exposed location experiencing high windspeeds and sea states. Personnel access to the turbine is a critical safety risk, yet is essential for the installation, commissioning and operational phases of the project.
The call aims to increase safety of personnel transfer operations while maximising opportunities for turbine access in the widest possible range of weather conditions to provide whole-life benefit to the project, minimising risk and avoiding delays. West of Orkney Windfarm is interested in innovative service operation vessel (SOV) design, as well as ancillary equipment.

The 1851 Royal Commission’s Industrial Fellowships provide up to £100,000 in funding to support graduates (science, engineering, medicine, design) in pursuing a PhD while working in industry.

scheme-raeng-research-chairs-senior-rese.text:
## Research Chairs and Senior Research Fellowships
The Research Chairs and Senior Research Fellowships scheme supports UK-based academics to deliver impactful engineering research in partnership with industry.
Applications are now closed.

## Support for applicants underrepresented in engineering
We offer personalised pre-application support from expert mentors to applicants from underrepresented groups.

## Submit an application
Submit and review the progress of your application via our Grant Management System.
• How to apply
• Eligibility
• FAQ
• Awardees

## About the scheme
The Research Chairs and Senior Research Fellowships scheme supports UK-based engineering academics to lead ambitious, applied research in collaboration with an industrial partner. Awardees receive £450,000 in Academy funding over five years, supported by additional contributions from their host organisation and an industry sponsor.
Funded by the UK Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) , the scheme brings together academic excellence and industrial innovation to address real-world engineering challenges – supporting research that leads to new products, processes and services with societal and economic benefit.
Please note that from 2026 the scheme will run as an annual call, with a single application round each year.

## Who is the scheme for?
The scheme is open to:
• UK-based academics working in any engineering discipline who are ready to lead a programme of collaborative research with an industry partner
Who are:
• Professors or an equivalent academic position
• Senior academics (lecturer/reader level or equivalent)

## Industry partnership
Prior to applying, applicants should have identified a collaborative research project and secured the support of an industrial sponsor.
See full eligibility criteria

## Supporting documents

## Contact us
If you have any questions about the programme, please contact the Research team.

## Why should I apply?
• Up to £450,000 over five years to establish or grow a leading research group
• Turn an existing industry relationship into a focused research programme
• Protected time for research with reduced teaching and administrative duties
• Part-time and flexible working options
• Training, networking and mentoring from leading engineers
• Size-dependent industry contribution (with cash or in-kind options available)

## Meet two of our awardees

## Video transcript
Our research sits at the very forefront of engineering and biology. So we're actually really, really good at treating water. The issue is it takes a lot of chemicals, a lot of energy, and simply is not sustainable economically or environmentally. Slow sand filtration is low cost and sustainable, but the issue is that it's also unreliable. With my background in environmental microbiology, we're now able to make slow sand filtration and biofiltration a reliable, sustainable solution for drinking water treatment. And of course, then this can be used globally because more than 800 million people are without access to clean drinking water. It's been a complete eye opener and really, really informative to work so closely with Scottish Water. They came to our monthly meetings and discussed real everyday industry challenges. So really this is a collaboration and a co-development of our research project that would not happen without the support of the Research Chair. As an engineer, my main duty or my moral responsibility would drive me to do what is needed to stop climate change. Highview technology is mainly for very large scale applications, which is needed for net zero 2050 because when we would have majority of energy generation from renewables and hence storage is essential. I was fortunate to be awarded this Royal Academy of Engineering Research Chair, which enabled me to grow the team from initially three, including myself, to 35 in five years. Without this scheme, I wouldn't be able to get what I'm getting today in terms of training next generation engineers and myself, my own success in terms of recognition. I get a lot more known by the community, not only in the UK but globally. And another indication is that I was elected to the Academy as a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2020, which is one of the biggest accomplishments I have. I would absolutely encourage anyone to apply for this scheme. It's been really essential to the growth and development of my career.

## Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to ensuring the Research Chairs and Senior Research Fellowships scheme is inclusive and accessible for academics across the UK. Engineering innovation is stronger when it reflects diverse experiences and perspectives, and we actively welcome applications from groups underrepresented in UK engineering.

## Support for underrepresented groups
Our Access Mentoring scheme provides tailored support and mentoring through the grant application process for applicants from the following groups:
• Women
• Black people (including any mixed ethnicity groups that include Black ethnic backgrounds)
• Disabled people
Please note that the deadline for applications submitted via our Access Mentoring scheme is 12 March at 4pm .
Find out more and request support

## See more opportunities for researchers
Find out more about our support for research.

## Celebrate successful industry-university collaborations
Our annual Bhattacharyya Award recognises sustained and impactful academia-industry partnerships.

## Global Talent Visa
The Global Talent visa is a UK immigration category for talented and promising individuals in specific sectors wishing to work in the UK.

scheme-lloyds-of-london-foundation-resea.text:
I could only confirm part of this. The guidelines document loaded, but my tool limit ran out before I could open any other page on www.lloyds.com. So the status, the dates and how to apply are all unconfirmed.

**Source checked:** https://www.lloyds.com/2026-grant-guidelines-and-criteria. This link opens a 3-page PDF called "Lloyd's of London Foundation Research Grant 2026 – Application Guidelines". The file's internal data says it was created on 15 July 2026.

**Round status and dates (not confirmed)**
- **Open now?** Unknown. The PDF gives no opening date, closing date or time.
- **Previous round:** No dates in the PDF. The text does say "Research Grant 2025" in section 1.1, which looks like a leftover from last year's version, so there was probably a 2025 round.
- **Next round:** Unknown. The PDF says "There will be one grant available in 2027". That suggests the 2026 call is choosing a grant to be paid in 2027, but the PDF doesn't say so directly.

**Who can apply** (same URL)
- It's open to individuals and organisations, "including (but not limited to)" university academics, research institutions, registered charities and think tanks, and (re)insurance industry participants (if the results are free and public).
- No career stage, years since PhD, nationality or country restriction is stated. Research can cover "both the UK and globally".

**Award** (same URL)
- **How many:** only one grant.
- **Size:** either a one-year project of about £100,000, or a project of up to two years at about £50,000 per year.
- **What it can pay for:** salary, direct costs, and overheads of no more than 18% of the total budget.

**Topic and assessment criteria** (same URL)
- **Focus:** risk understanding linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and climate change adaptation and mitigation, for example "fire, flood, drought, changes to weather patterns and other natural disasters".
- **What they want to see:** new research on UK or global risks, a clear link to the financial side of risk, and a route to practical impact through work with stakeholders.
- **Automatic rejection if:** the work would have an immediate commercial outcome, there's no clear method, it lacks academic excellence, or there's no engagement with non-academic stakeholders.

**What you must submit**
- The PDF doesn't give the application form, page or word limits, CV format, letters, statements or any internal selection step.
- The only content it requires is a communications plan. This must cover audience, route to market and timescale. It must also credit the Foundation as funder, allow for joint promotion with them, and accept that they approve all external communications.
- **After the award:** a 3–5 page report 12 months after payment, covering delivery against objectives, challenges and a detailed breakdown of spending. You may also be asked to give a presentation.

**How well it fits you:** only partly. It isn't really an ocean-waves call. It could work if you frame the project as coastal flooding or extreme-wave risk with a clear financial or insurance angle and non-academic partners. With one grant of about £100k available, it's worth applying only if the timing suits you.

**Next steps**
1. Open the Foundation's research grant page on lloyds.com to find the deadline and application form. I couldn't fetch it.
2. Ask the Foundation by email whether the 2026 call (for the 2027 grant) is still open.

scheme-catapult-researcher-in-residence.text:
I could only partly confirm the scheme's current state. The single round I found closed on 31 August 2026, and the projects are now running. I found nothing about a next round.

I read one page, https://innovationlaunchpad.group.shef.ac.uk/rirsprint/, but the copy I got was saved on **2026-08-05**, not today. My tool limit ran out before I could read the home page, news, terms or Catapult contact pages, so anything posted since early August is missing.

**Is a round open now?**
- No. The page says "The call for the Researchers in Residence Sprint programme is open now", but that was true on 5 August. — /rirsprint/
- Closing date: "by 23:59 (UTC+1) on 31 August 2026", with applications sent by email to rirapplications@amrc.co.uk. That date has passed. — /rirsprint/
- Opening date: not given. The "Timeline" heading has no text in the copy I read (it may be an image), so I can't confirm it. — /rirsprint/
- Other dates: award letters "in September"; projects have a "fixed start on 01 October 2026" and "must be fully completed by 28th February 2027". There are "no flexibility or opportunity for extension". — /rirsprint/

**Previous round**
- None that I could find. This is the first Sprint round. Its funding is described as "an additional £500,000" from EPSRC for a programme "running between October 2026 and February 2027". It builds on the Network's longer-running Researchers in Residence scheme, whose round dates I couldn't check. — /rirsprint/

**Next round**
- Not announced on the page I read. The fixed one-off budget and fixed dates suggest a single call, but I can't confirm that. — /rirsprint/

**Who can apply**
- The applicant must be the person doing the placement. — /rirsprint/
- You must "hold a PhD (or demonstrate experience and knowledge to a similar degree)" and be employed full- or part-time at a UK university for the whole placement. — /rirsprint/
- There is no limit on career stage or years since PhD. The page says "first time applicants with great ideas and relevant experience are welcomed". — /rirsprint/
- Nationality: the scheme sets no rule, but "some Catapults have restrictions on nationalities that they can collaborate with". You need to check with your host. — /rirsprint/
- At least one Catapult must host the project, and the proposal must be "co-developed with the host Catapult". — /rirsprint/

**Award amount and length**
- £25,000–£50,000 of university researcher costs, paid to your university. — /rirsprint/
- It covers 100% of direct staff costs (salary, pension, employer's National Insurance, apprenticeship levy) and direct other costs such as travel, consumables and software. Overheads are not allowed. — /rirsprint/
- The project runs about five months, from 1 October 2026 to 28 February 2027. — /rirsprint/

**What you must submit and do**
1. Talk to a contact at your proposed host Catapult first. This is required. — /rirsprint/
2. Send your university's legal team the Catapult's Collaboration Agreement template early. A signed agreement is needed before you start. — /rirsprint/
3. Ask for the application form by emailing rirapplications@amrc.co.uk with a short outline of your idea and the Catapult you spoke to. The form isn't public, so I can't confirm its sections or page and word limits. — /rirsprint/
4. Sections the guidance names:
   - Fit with the Network's priorities (Net Zero, Healthcare and Wellbeing, Resilience), including links to EPSRC research areas
   - Up to five deliverables
   - Impact on the UK economy and society, and how you will engage users
   - Costs
   
   — /rirsprint/
5. A letter of support from your university. It must:
   - confirm the signatory has read the terms and the collaboration agreement template
   - state the institution's support for you
   - say how the project helps the institution's strategy
   - give a cost breakdown calculated by usual procedures
   - be signed by someone with authority over your time
   
   — /rirsprint/
6. Optional diversity monitoring form after you submit. — /rirsprint/
- CV format: not stated. I can't confirm whether a CV is needed, but "track record" is one of the review criteria. — /rirsprint/
- Internal selection at your university: not mentioned. — /rirsprint/
- Review process: at least two independent reviewers, a chance to respond to their comments, then a panel from the Catapult Network, EPSRC and the Network+. — /rirsprint/

**Fit for you (my judgement)**
- Topic fit is strong to core if the Offshore Renewable Energy Catapult hosted you, since that falls under Net Zero. Career stage is ideal and you appear eligible. The effort is moderate.
- As things stand it isn't actionable, because the only known round has closed. I would not put it on your short list until a new round is announced.
- To do: email rirapplications@amrc.co.uk to ask whether there will be another Sprint round or a main Researchers in Residence round.
- To do: start talking to the Offshore Renewable Energy Catapult now, so you're ready if a round opens.

scheme-istructe-research-award.text:
I could only confirm part of what you asked for. The IStructE Research Award page has no dates on it, so I can't tell you whether a round is open now. My tool-use limit ran out before I could reach the application form or any other IStructE page.

**Notes** (all from https://www.istructe.org/training-and-development/apply-for-grants/research-award/, unless marked otherwise)

**Round status and dates**
- **Open now?** Not confirmed. The page gives no opening date, closing date, time or "open/closed" status.
- **Previous round:** Not confirmed. No past round dates appear on the page.
- **How often:** The page says the Research Fund "awards grants every two years". That is the only clue to when the next round comes. I haven't found any past round dates to count forward from, so I can't estimate the next one.

**Who can apply**
- **Career stage:** Any. The page says "Research can be conducted by an individual or group at any career stage". There's no limit on years since PhD.
- **Who applies:** "Either a university researcher or industrial partner may apply".
- **Partners:** The form must be "completed and signed by both an industry and academic partner". Part of the research must happen within a university.
- **Nationality or country:** The page sets no rule. The only stated condition is that you apply in English.

**Money and duration**
- **Amount:** £6,000, paid as "£5,000 upfront and £1,000 on delivery of a project summary".
- **Duration:** Not stated.
- **What academic partners can spend it on:** materials, test equipment, software, travel (capped at "less than £1,000") and salary for a researcher or lab technician.
- **Industry partners:** They can spend it on equipment and software, but not on staff costs.
- **Split:** Funding can be divided between the partners, though most is likely to go to the academic partner.

**What you must submit**
- One application form, in English, signed by both the industry and the academic partner.
- If the work is part of a larger project, you must say exactly which part the grant will pay for.
- Not confirmed: the form's sections, page or word limits, CV format, letters or statements, and any internal selection step. None of these are on the page.

**How applications are judged**
- **Main criteria:** technical quality, and how far the project builds a working relationship between research and industry partners (new or existing).
- **Additional criteria:** impact to industry, benefit to IStructE members, benefit to society, and value for money.
- The page also encourages pilot studies that wouldn't attract normal Research Council funding.
- You may be asked to present at IStructE events, but this isn't a condition of the award.
